title: Validation of Specialized Dosimetry Software for Selective Internal Radiation Therapy (SIRT) in Patients with Liver Malignancies
summary:
Background
Patients with malignant liver tumors may undergo a treatment in which tiny radioactive beads are delivered directly into the liver through the blood vessels. The aim is to target and destroy tumor tissue with radiation. A specialized computer software called HERMIA is used to plan and verify this treatment. This study aims to investigate how accurately this software can calculate the distribution of radiation.

Research Question
The aim of this study is to determine whether the predicted distribution of radioactive beads before treatment corresponds to their actual distribution after treatment. In addition, the study will investigate whether the software's calculations can help predict treatment success, survival, and possible side effects.

Methodology
For participating patients, imaging examinations performed as part of their routine treatment will be evaluated before and after therapy. Before treatment, the planned distribution of radioactive beads will be calculated using medical imaging. Within 24 hours after treatment, another imaging examination will be performed to assess the actual distribution. Both results will be analyzed and compared using the HERMIA software.

In addition, disease progression, tumor response to treatment, and possible side effects will be documented during routine follow-up examinations.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients undergoing SIRT evaluation at our institution who are eligible for study participation.
No clinically significant ascites and adequate liver function:
Bilirubin < 2 mg/dL.
Albumin >escape> 3 g/dL.
AST/ALT (GOT/GPT) < 5 times the upper limit of normal.
Adequate renal function (GFR > 30 mL/min).
Lung shunt dose < 30 Gy.
Exclusion criteria:
Contradictions in the inclusion criteria
